_doc: Per-hook p95 latency budgets in milliseconds (documentation data).
_methodology: Each hook is fired repeatedly against a representative fixture; the p95 duration is compared against budget * multiplier. session-start-orient.sh's 2000ms budget was established (not previously benched) 2026-07-30: an ubuntu:24.04 Docker container (read-only mount, mirrors the ubuntu-latest CI runner) gave raw p50/p95 ~56-58/59-70ms across 3x n=50 runs (telemetry-adjusted floors to 0) -- comfortably under budget. A Windows dev box with an empty TMPDIR gave adjusted p50/p95 ~395-401/482-496ms across 3x n=100 runs -- also comfortably under budget, confirming 2000ms rather than guessing it. The SAME Windows box with its real (~88k-entry) TMPDIR, littered by an unrelated project sharing the machine's system temp dir, measured adjusted p95 ~4912ms (OVER) -- traced to this hook's stale-tracker sweep, which at the time scanned the ENTIRE shared temp root on every fire with no scoping. FIXED 2026-07-31 (hooks/_tmpdir.sh): every hook tracker now lives in a scoped dir we own, and the sweep runs three passes -- the scoped dir every fire (bounded by OUR churn), the POSIX per-uid lock dirs, and the legacy shared-root sweep gated behind a stamp checked with -mtime +7 (nominally weekly, in practice every 8 days). Post-fix on the same littered box: adjusted p50/p95 489/539ms, and a bare `perf-bench` exits 0 with no TMPDIR override. Disposition changed accordingly: an over-budget session-start-orient reading is NO LONGER dismissable as dev-box litter. It now means one of (a) the sample caught the ~weekly legacy sweep, which still scans the shared root once and is a KNOWN outlier -- a single fire in an n=100 sample cannot move p95, so suspect this only for a p50 shift; or (b) harness_tmp fell back to the shared root (scoped dir unwritable or squatted), which is a real regression worth chasing. PERF_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER remains the knob for genuinely slow machines (CI already sets it). See .superpowers/sdd/2026-07-28-v038-independent-items/perf-budget-report.md for the pre-fix samples.
_multiplier: Local default 1.0; CI raises PERF_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER to absorb runner variance.
